_readme: FIAT FIGHT KIT, THE TEST (17 Oct, Matt): one pair of hands for each kind (a bat, a pump shotgun, a bullpup, a carbine, a crossbow, a big revolver, a knife, a garage rifle), the Parade's plate and wall at the new size, the four tile icons. Judge these in the frame before the set is run.

Run: godot --headless --script res://tools/pixellab_batch_v2.gd ++ --manifest res://tools/pixellab_fight_kit_test_manifest.json   (++ --dry-run to list; one that came out wrong: ++ --only <name> ++ --force)
Hands: art/fight/hands/<base>.png, 280x210, styled on the base's item art and framed on the kind's current hands; the code looks a base up first, the kind's picture its fallback.

Walls and plates: art/fight_new/<site>_cover.png 744x173 and _plate.png 744x320, the largest the API takes at their shape (the bigger frame draws them at 950 wide, scaling x1.28); the live ones in art/fight/ stay until these are judged. Run the test's Parade pair first: it shows the size is taken.
Icons: art/ui_new/their_fire, kills, armour, rounds - 64x64, drawn at 36 px on the run's tiles beside Matt's dps and hp. Never written over art/ui.

jobs.description: First-person view of the player's own two hands in fingerless wool gloves holding a crossbow, shouldered, the bow's limbs wide across the frame, the bolt pointing forward up the frame, coming in from the bottom right corner of the frame, as in a light-gun arcade game; the sleeves of a worn work jacket at the wrists. Exactly the weapon in the style image, its shape and colours. Only the hands and what they hold, coming in from the bottom right edge. Realistic painted pixel art, soft overcast light, muted cool northern palette, worn and lived-in, post-collapse Britain on a grey day; no black outlines, not anime, not a cartoon, not glossy; no text, no logos.
jobs._where: your hands: Crossbow (primary; falls back to hands_improvised)

jobs.description: A first-person view at crouching eye level, as if from behind cover in a light-gun arcade game, looking along a parade of shops on an estate: shutters down and sprayed, a bookie's and a chippy and a launderette, a bus shelter with its glass out, a car burnt out at the kerb, an alley between two shops. Nobody in the scene, empty and waiting. Composed for three figures to stand in later: clear open ground in the middle distance just right of centre, a dark doorway or gap on the left side well down the scene, and room in the right foreground. The ground runs across the lower third; the horizon sits a third of the way down. One continuous scene edge to edge: no repeated sections, no seams. The bottom fifth of the scene is plain open ground running to the frame's edge, nothing standing in the foreground: no walls, rubble or cover there, it is drawn over later. Realistic painted pixel art, soft overcast light, muted cool northern palette, worn and lived-in, post-collapse Britain on a grey day; no black outlines, not anime, not a cartoon, not glossy; no text, no logos.
jobs._where: the plate at the frame's drawn size: the_parade (the live art/fight/the_parade_plate.png its style)

jobs.description: Seen very close from behind, running unbroken across the whole width of the frame at the bottom: a low wall of grimy red brick with a broken concrete coping, moss in the joints, a weed growing from a crack, as the cover a player crouches behind in a light-gun arcade game. One continuous piece edge to edge, no repeated sections, no seams. Only the cover, nothing above or behind it; its top edge uneven, filling the lower two thirds of the image. No packaging, signs or anything with lettering on it. Realistic painted pixel art, soft overcast light, muted cool northern palette, worn and lived-in, post-collapse Britain on a grey day; no black outlines, not anime, not a cartoon, not glossy; no text, no logos.
jobs._where: the wall at the frame's drawn size: the_parade
